text:
Willing misery
Outlives incertain pomp, is crowned before;
The one is filling still, never complete,
The other, at high wish. Best state, contentless,
Hath a distracted and most wretched being,
Worse than the worst, content.
plain: Wanting more never fills you up. Someone with little who is at peace beats someone with everything who is never satisfied.

text: The middle of humanity thou never knewest, but the extremity of both ends.
plain: You only know the top and the bottom. Learn the steady middle.

text: There is no time so miserable but a man may be true.
plain: Hard times never excuse being fake. You can always stay honest.

text:
What viler thing upon the earth than friends
Who can bring noblest minds to basest ends!
plain: False friends can drag a good person down faster than any enemy.

text: Promising is the very air o’ th’ time; it opens the eyes of expectation.
plain: People hand out promises like air. Do the thing instead and you stand out.

text:
Then do we sin against our own estate
When we may profit meet and come too late.
plain: Let a good opening pass and you wrong yourself. Move while it's open.

text:
At all times alike
Men are not still the same: ’twas time and griefs
That framed him thus.
plain: People are not fixed. Time and pain shape them, and time can heal what it bent.

text:
Crimes, like lands,
Are not inherited.
plain: You don't owe for what someone before you did. Neither does anyone else.

text: Let it go naked. Men may see’t the better.
plain: Plain truth, undressed, is easiest to see.

text:
You should have feared false times when you did feast,
Suspect still comes where an estate is least.
plain: Doubt and suspicion show up when you're broke, which is when it's too late. Watch people while times are good.

text:
Wilt thou draw near the nature of the gods?
Draw near them then in being merciful.
Sweet mercy is nobility’s true badge.
plain: Mercy is what makes a strong person noble.

text:
Give me a staff of honour for mine age,
But not a sceptre to control the world.
plain: Pick respect over rule. A walking staff beats a scepter.

text:
Then give me leave, for losers will have leave
To ease their stomachs with their bitter tongues.
plain: People who lost something need to say it out loud. Let them, and let yourself.

text:
Sorrow concealed, like an oven stopped,
Doth burn the heart to cinders where it is.
plain: Pain you keep sealed up burns you from the inside. Talk, write, let it out.

text:
To weep with them that weep doth ease some deal,
But sorrow flouted at is double death.
plain: Shared sorrow helps. Being laughed at in your sorrow is twice as bad.

text:
If there were reason for these miseries,
Then into limits could I bind my woes.
plain: Grief has no logic, so don't expect yourself to reason your way out of it.

text:
Why, foolish Lucius, dost thou not perceive
That Rome is but a wilderness of tigers?
plain: Sometimes being thrown out of a bad place is a lucky break.
We're not giants, we're tough, and we're carrying more than anyone should.

text:
Why, I have not another tear to shed.
Besides, this sorrow is an enemy,
And would usurp upon my watery eyes,
And make them blind with tributary tears.
plain: Grief can blind you. At some point you have to stop crying and decide what to do.

text:
I was about to tell thee: when my heart,
As wedged with a sigh, would rive in twain,
Lest Hector or my father should perceive me,
I have, as when the sun doth light a storm,
Buried this sigh in wrinkle of a smile.
But sorrow that is couch’d in seeming gladness
Is like that mirth fate turns to sudden sadness.
plain: You can smile over a heavy chest, but hidden sorrow only turns sharper.

text:
Why should I war without the walls of Troy
That find such cruel battle here within?
Each Trojan that is master of his heart,
Let him to field; Troilus, alas! hath none.
plain: There's no use winning outside while you're losing the fight inside. Master yourself first.

text: He that will have a cake out of the wheat must tarry the grinding.
plain: Anything worth having has steps you can't skip. Wait through the grinding.

text:
Things won are done; joy’s soul lies in the doing.
That she belov’d knows naught that knows not this:
Men prize the thing ungain’d more than it is.
plain: The chase is sweeter than the catch. We overvalue what we haven't got yet.

text: Well, the gods are above; time must friend or end.
plain: Time will settle it one way or the other. Do what you can and let it work.

text: Keep it, I cannot eat it.
plain: Gold doesn't fill you up. Know what money can't buy.
